title: apricitus migrate: today's files into a library
description:
Implement `design/storage.md` §5 as `apricitus migrate --from <repo root> --to <library> [--link]` (in `apricitus-data`, exposed by `apricitus-cli`).

## Behaviour
- Recordings, Clips (+ analysis attachments; audio cloned or hard-linked), Slices, Markers, Candidates (with `legacyId`), Verdicts (`judge: "local"`), Crates, and Scores with ScoreRefs.
- A report of counts.
- Exits non-zero on any unresolved score reference.
- Idempotent: a second run reports 0 changes.

## Check
`scripts/check-migration.sh` migrates to a temp library, then for each `examples/*.apr|yaml` renders it from the files (`apricitus render`) and from the library (`apricitus render --library <lib>`), and `cmp`s the WAVs.

## Verify
```
apricitus migrate --from . --to /tmp/apr-lib --link     # report
apricitus migrate --from . --to /tmp/apr-lib --link     # "0 changes"
scripts/check-migration.sh                              # all identical
```

---
**Repo:** `~/Projects/Ripple`, branch `master` (don't switch).
**Toolchain:** `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH`; Python `analysis/.venv/bin/python`; web `cd web && npm …`.
**Protocol:** initiative `apricitus-e70662`: specs first; log with `kbs comment`; run **Verify** and paste the output tail; label `ready-for-review`; never commit, push, close, or deploy. Don't change visuals in `web/src/ui/*` (the web session owns them); data calls only.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Root cause of check-migration.sh 'WAVs differ': not float precision. (1) the script's 'if ! cd $REPO && apricity render' parses as '(! cd) && render', so the from-files render never ran and cmp compared a missing file; (2) compiled Timelines from files vs library are identical except the audio path. Rewrote the script, migration.rs (real ids, recordings per piece, stems, aliases, analysis sha, candidates via candidate_id, markers, ScoreRefs, verdicts/crates from library/*.json) and the loader (annotations.clips key, aliases, paging). Scratch tests removed. Writing tests next.
